chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] Greatnesses who [went forth] against the Darkness.
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is overwhelmingly dominant. The chapter consists of two linked but potentially independent teachings: (1) a five-fold enumeration of the greatnesses (¶2-9) with systematic emanation hierarchy, and (2) five advent similes with cosmic interpretation (¶10-29). Gardner notes the second section is 'in effect a separate and unrelated kephalaion.' The similes use natural correspondences (noble son, judge, king inspecting craftsmen, fig-garden, butter in milk) to map cosmic processes — classic correspondential teaching method where both sides stay within the system. Only the opening dialogue formula (¶1) and closing beatitude (¶30) are clearly later layers. The 'Now, just as' formulas in ¶15 and ¶21 are simile-completion structures integral to the teaching, not editorial seams — they map analogy→cosmic entity with no institutional content. Gardner's note that Jesus the Splendour as fifth greatness 'may be a later development' is worth noting but at the textual level ¶7 follows the same enumeration pattern as ¶2-6.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the Darkness, it was defeated by five greatnesses.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula 'Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:' — standard hagiographic attribution wrapper.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic mixed paragraph: dialogue frame formula wrapping a substantive cosmological topic statement. The teaching content introduces the five-fold structure that the chapter will develop.

paragraphs.core_text: The first greatness is the Father of Greatness who exists in calm and hiddenness; as he is established in his light-earth, in his own essence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Maps the first greatness to its cosmic attributes: calm, hiddenness, light-earth, own essence. Both sides of every mapping are within the cosmic system. The substrate vocabulary score (12.0) confirms cosmological register.

paragraphs.core_text: Four greatnesses were manifested and came forth of him. They were appointed to ten parts, and established in total twelve.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural-mathematical accounting of the emanation system. Gardner calls the twelve-part calculation 'undoubtedly forced,' but the content remains within cosmic architecture — counting emanated entities. No vocabulary leaves the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second greatness poured out and was manifested. It was revealed from the first greatness. It is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, together with the First Man and his five sons; these are the second greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Emanation language ('poured out and was manifested,' 'revealed from') is systematic process vocabulary. Maps the second greatness to its cosmic constituents.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.50⟩
The third greatness is the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder, the Living Spirit, and the five sons of the Living Spirit. These are the third greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. High substrate score (58.62) — dense with cosmic entity names. Systematic listing of the creation-phase emanation hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth greatness is the Third Ambassador, and the Pillar of Glory, and all the light powers who were revealed from him. These are the fourth greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration unit. Same syntactic pattern as ¶4-5. Maps the fourth greatness to the ascent-phase emanation hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth greatness who came from the Father is Jesus the Splendour, and all his powers whom he summoned, his emanations who were [...] They poured out and were manifested from him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth enumeration unit. Gardner notes Jesus the Splendour as fifth greatness 'may be a later development of Manichaean doctrine.' However, the text follows the identical enumeration pattern and emanation vocabulary as ¶2-6. At the textual level, this is structurally integral to the five-fold teaching. Classified as substrate with this uncertainty flagged.

paragraphs.core_text: This is, so that they were spread out and [...] fives: these five [sons] of the First Man [...] the entire building; another five are the five sons of the Living Spirit who are spread out to five places, supporting [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentadic distribution — mapping how the cosmic sons are spread to their five cosmic places. Systematic spatial cosmology. Heavy lacunae but the visible text is entirely within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] total in twelve parts that [... There are] another two added to them who are the summons and the obedience. They are the father and the mother whom Jesus the Splendour by his advent has appointed as successors to his place [...] the great earth and the [...] in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the dodecadic accounting. The summons and obedience are cosmic entities. 'Appointed as successors to his place' describes cosmic role assignment, not institutional succession. Both sides within the cosmic system despite heavy damage.

paragraphs.core_text: [The advent ...] of the First Man who came [...] belonging to [...] existing in a kingdom [...] esteem before they who belong to his household [...] his enemies [...] and suffering by their wickedness; and they take from him [...] and a richness; and they imprison [him in] captivity and take from him their companies (?). Yet, he [...] by his humility; and he takes heart and restrains his enemy [...] in silence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The 'noble son' simile for the advent of the First Man. This is correspondential teaching through analogy — a natural situation mapping a cosmic process. Both sides (the noble son's situation and the First Man's descent) stay within the cosmic narrative. The simile is integral to the teaching structure: simile (¶10) → cosmic mapping (¶11).

paragraphs.core_text: Just as with this man, this noble son whose enemies surround him, this also is how the advent of the First Man happened, [...] rulers, the enemies of the light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Interpretive key connecting the noble son simile to the cosmic event. 'The rulers, the enemies of the light' maps the analogy squarely onto cosmic entities.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, the advent of the Living Spirit and the commandment that he received, whereby he came upon all the rulers, it differs from that of the First Man. His advent [...] the advent of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural transition introducing the second advent. The teaching compares the Living Spirit's advent to the First Man's — a cosmic-to-cosmic contrast. This is systematic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.51⟩
The advent of the Living Spirit is like this, when he was sent from the greatness that he might bring up the First Man. He resembles a judge the king would send to overturn the violence to that man, the noble son against whom his enemies sinned. And he, this judge, [...] hard and cruel [...] and he gives the means [...] by his righteousness and his strength; and he also judges all who are condemned according to their rebellious heart, and repays each according to his deserts. They who are worthy of blows he strikes with hard leather whips. Again, these who are worthy of cutting off their limbs, or indeed their [...] and he repays them accordingly. [...] and he binds and fetters them, and hangs by [...] and thus he does to them with a righteous judgement. And he kills them to flay their skin [...] so that they will be killed by a death [...] until they die. Again, [they for] whom it is fitting [...] to banish from their dwellings he may remove according to a righteous judgement; just as they had faulted and sinned against the noble son.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended judge simile for the Living Spirit. The graduated punishments (blows, cutting limbs, binding, flaying, banishment) describe what the cosmic judge DOES — this is correspondential teaching mapping judicial action onto cosmic process. No side of the mapping leaves the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the associates in the mystery and the assistants of this judge, these who belong to him in great strength; in an instant and haste they shall do the will of their master.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the judge simile — the judge's assistants correspond to the Living Spirit's cosmic helpers. Still within the simile framework.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as this genuine judge, who was sent from the king to overturn the violence to this man, the noble son: this is also the case with the Living Spirit. He also was sent from the King of the lights to overturn the vengeance and violence to the First Man, against whom the King of the realms of Darkness had sinned. He faulted and sinned against him, and also his rebellious powers. Therefore, when (the Living Spirit) came, he bore up the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: SEAM FLAG IS FALSE POSITIVE. The 'Now, just as' is a simile-completion formula integral to the teaching pattern (simile → 'just as X, so also Y' → cosmic mapping). Both sides map within the cosmic system: judge→Living Spirit, king→King of the lights, noble son→First Man, enemies→King of the realms of Darkness. No institutional vocabulary present despite the flag. The institutional score (3.53) appears to be noise.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, all the rulers, the powers of sin who had faulted and sinned against the sons of the First Man, he has judged them according to a righteous judgement. He has bound them in heaven and earth. He put each one to the place fitting for him; he weighed each of them according to his cruelty and oppression. While some of them he enclosed in the prison, others he hung head down. Some [...] are crucified, others are sat down all the time. Some among them are fixed beneath their associates, restricted by a strong chain; others he made the holders of authority over their companions beneath, so that they may do their pleasure amongst these below them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic judgement of the rulers — describes how the Living Spirit distributed the defeated cosmic powers into their cosmic positions (bound in heaven and earth, enclosed, hung head down, crucified, chained). This is systematic cosmic process: each punishment corresponds to a cosmic position. Classic substrate mapping of judgement onto cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: when the Father of Life established the judgements [...] He was revealed to all the powers of Darkness. He judged them as a true giver of judgement [...] This is the first judgement that the Living Spirit gave the rulers [in respect of the] First Man. Indeed, he gave victory to the First Man corresponding to his victory; but he condemned the King of the realms of Darkness corresponding to that by which he had erred.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Happen you know this [...] that' — direct audience address, dialogue frame marker. The dialogue_frame score (4.82) confirms pedagogical framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mixed: dialogue address formula ('Happen you know this') wraps substrate teaching about the first cosmic judgement. The core content describes the Living Spirit's judgement in cosmic-correspondential terms: 'corresponding to his victory,' 'corresponding to that by which he had erred' — these are precise correspondential formulas mapping action to consequence within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] this chain, of this sort, became [...] the earth till the end time when the universe will be dissolved; and it perishes in the great fire and is separated. While the light goes to its country, the Darkness remains in the chain and fetter for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic eschatology — describes the final separation of light and Darkness. Both sides within the cosmic system: light→its country, Darkness→chain and fetter. The chain imagery corresponds to the cosmic binding described in ¶16.

paragraphs.core_text: The advent also of the Third Ambassador, when he came to inspect they who are imprisoned in the zone: he is like a great king who comes and inspects craftsmen [...] and [...] and [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces the Third Ambassador's advent with the king-inspecting-craftsmen simile. 'The zone' is cosmic geography. The simile maps cosmic inspection onto a natural analogy.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, they who are good, of the craftsmen and architects and artisans whom he has there in each place: he shall see that they have worked well, and have fallen to his works in their fashion. He shall rejoice with great joy [...] He shall thank the artisans who have constructed his works [and completed] his orders.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the king/craftsmen simile. The craftsmen and artisans correspond to the cosmic builders (the gods who constructed the cosmos). The simile describes cosmic satisfaction with the created order.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as this great king who comes and inspects his works and fortifications, so also is the advent of the Third Ambassador. For, when he too came, he saw [his works] established and prepared and [...] series of the rulers prepared and established there, above and below, outside and within, in the great pattern that his brothers had made. They had come before him to the contest, they who had fixed and created the universe before he came. He saw the gods and the angels established and controlling the fortifications [...] guarding the entire ruling-power [...] which his first powers had done. They are the First Man and the Living Spirit and the Great Spirit, the Mother of Life.
paragraphs.temporal_note: SEAM FLAG IS FALSE POSITIVE. Same simile-completion formula as ¶15. 'Now, just as X, so also Y' maps king→Third Ambassador, fortifications→cosmic architecture, craftsmen→First Man/Living Spirit/Mother of Life. Every entity is cosmic. Institutional vocabulary score is 0.0. The seam detector fired on the bridge connective alone. The content describes the Third Ambassador surveying the cosmic order 'above and below, outside and within' — pure cosmic geography.

paragraphs.core_text: Therefore, when he saw them, that they had created everything with great wisdom, [...] as they looked he plundered (?) [...] in his advent, by which he came, he was unveiled to them. He says to the Living Spirit: "The judgement that you have [...] good, what you uttered [...] you gave to them correspondingly; so that they were moved and raised up to that of which they were not worthy".
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Third Ambassador addresses the Living Spirit — cosmic entity speaking to cosmic entity. 'You gave to them correspondingly' uses explicit correspondential language. The speech is within the cosmic drama, not editorial frame.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.53⟩
The advent also of Jesus the Splendour, the time when he came to all [...] being just like a man if he is sent to pull out a [...] burn a difficult fig-garden with fire. Therefore, again, when he has first cut the bad trees with his axe and has pulled out [...] and their body with his fire, so that they should not return to sprout from this time, nor bear fruit bad to eat [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: The fig-garden simile for Jesus the Splendour's advent. The tree/fire imagery has NT resonance (Matt 3:10, 7:17-18) but there is NO citation formula — the simile describes cosmic purification through natural analogy. The 'bad trees' correspond to cosmic powers, not contemporary institutions. The teaching method (natural correspondence for cosmic process) is consistent with the chapter's substrate pattern.

paragraphs.core_text: Afterwards, he also planted good plants: the tree of life that will make good fruit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the tree simile — destruction of bad trees followed by planting of the tree of life. 'The tree of life' is a cosmic entity, not a citation. Both sides within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is like this simile of the advent of Jesus the Splendour. It happened like this; because he too set out [...] his power and his wisdom, in his [...]-ness [...] a king and a saviour [...] in his glorious wisdom he destroyed them. He bound and crushed them like the fire that shall burn and destroy trees. This is also how he performed his will in the zone, among the many powers, until he reached the form of the flesh of Adam and Eve, the first humans. [He perfected] his will in Eve, he [...] He also gave hope to Adam, and the good news [...] glorious [...] He went up to the heights [...] of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the tree simile onto the cosmic narrative of Jesus the Splendour's work: destroying powers in the zone, reaching Adam and Eve, ascending to the heights. All cosmic events. 'The zone' is cosmic geography. Adam and Eve are cosmological figures (the first humans in the cosmic drama), not historical persons.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.54⟩
Then the summons and the obedience, the great counsel that came to the elements, which are set in conjunction: it mixed with them, it was established in silence. It bears up [...] until the end time when it can arise and stand firm in the great fire. It will gather to it its own soul, and sculpt it in the Last Statue. You will also find it sweeps out and casts from it the pollution that is foreign to it. However, the life and the light that are in all things it gathers in to it, and builds upon its body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the cosmic function of the summons and obedience — mixing with elements, gathering soul into the Last Statue, separating pollution from light. Pure cosmic process. 'You will also find' is a pedagogical convention within the teaching voice, not an editorial address. The Last Statue doctrine is systematic cosmic eschatology: body-building as cosmic gathering.

paragraphs.core_text: The time when this Last Statue will be perfect in all its limbs, then it can become free and ascend from that great struggle through the Living Spirit its father, the one who comes and brings a [...] limb. He brings it up from within this gathering (?), the melting down and destruction of all things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the Last Statue cosmic eschatology. The Statue ascending through the Living Spirit, the melting down and destruction of all things — pure cosmic process vocabulary. 'Perfect in all its limbs' is body-cosmos correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this counsel, that summons and obedience, resembles thus cooled butter. If a person will take and set it in hot milk, it melts down and soaks in with this hot milk. It melts in another time in silence and quiet to the midst [...] yet also, of the power and the taste of this milk [...] is drawn to (the butter), and (the milk) sets and becomes cold [...] in [...] and the [...] this milk it shall clarify and discard. However, the oil and the grease and the 'beauty' of the milk it shall gather in to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The butter-in-milk simile — a remarkable natural correspondence for the cosmic process of the summons and obedience. Butter melting into hot milk, absorbing its essence, then separating = the summons mixing with elements, gathering light, separating from pollution. This is classic correspondential teaching: natural process mapping cosmic process. Both sides within the system.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.55⟩
Again, this too is what the advent of that thought is like, the counsel of life, which is the summons and obedience that came to the elements. This is the one that at the end can arise and stand firm, and will gather in to it all the lives, and the light that has remained behind in everything. It can build them upon its body; it will gather them in to it [...] in its image for ever and ever [...] from this time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the butter simile back to the cosmic entity (summons and obedience). 'Gather in to it all the lives, and the light that has remained behind in everything' — cosmic eschatological gathering process. 'Build them upon its body' — body-cosmos correspondence. Minor exhortation score (3.53) likely from 'for ever and ever' — a cosmic duration marker, not devotional closure.

Classic beatitude closure formula: 'Blessed is every one who will believe in these five advents and be confirmed in the knowledge.' This is the devotional wrapper appended to the substrate teaching sequence. The seam flag correctly identifies this as editorial extension. The formula addresses the community ('every one who will believe'), pivoting from cosmic exposition to audience application. Exhortation score (15.62) confirms.
